# MSA Review — RadialSpark, LLC (Vendor) / Clear Capital (Customer)

**Bottom line:** This is a vendor-drafted agreement with several provisions that are materially off-market against the customer. The highest-priority issues are (1) IP ownership conditioned on payment with no assignment language, (2) a liability cap that is not reciprocal in substance and swallows the IP indemnity, (3) no indemnification obligation running to Company at all (Section 7's heading promises "Indemnification of Contractor," and Section 9 — the carve-out referenced in the cap — is actually the Independent Contractor clause), (4) unilateral rate increases, (5) no data security / privacy obligations despite Clear Capital's business, and (6) an arbitration clause with an obscure provider, no seat, and an attorneys' fee waiver.

---

## Tier 1 — Do Not Sign Without Fixing

### 1. Broken cross-reference guts the liability cap carve-out (¶7(a))
The cap is unlimited "except with respect to Contractor's obligations pursuant to Paragraph 9." Paragraph 9 is **Independent Contractor** — not indemnification (there is no Contractor indemnity anywhere). So the carve-out is meaningless, and Contractor's total liability, including for IP infringement, confidentiality breach, and gross negligence, is capped at fees paid for the specific SOW.

**Fix:** Add a Contractor indemnity (below) and rewrite the carve-out:
> "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the limitations in this Paragraph 7 shall not apply to: (i) Contractor's indemnification obligations under Paragraph [new]; (ii) breach of Paragraph 8 (Confidential Information) or Paragraph [new] (Data Security); (iii) Contractor's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; (iv) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d) (Anti-Corruption); or (v) death, bodily injury, or damage to tangible property caused by Contractor."

### 2. No indemnity in Company's favor (¶5(c), ¶7)
Contractor *warrants* non-infringement (¶5(c)) but there is no obligation to defend or indemnify. A warranty without an indemnity means Company funds its own defense against a third-party claim and can only recover capped damages.

**Fix:** Insert:
> "Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates, officers, directors and employees from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting losses, damages, liabilities, settlements, and reasonable attorneys' fees and costs, arising from: (a) any allegation that the Works, Services, Contractor Information, or third-party materials supplied by Contractor infringe or misappropriate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret or other intellectual property right; (b) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 8 or its data security obligations; (c) Contractor's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (d) any claim by Contractor personnel for employment status, wages, taxes, or benefits from Company; and (e) Contractor's breach of Paragraph 5(d). Company shall provide prompt notice and reasonable cooperation; Contractor shall not settle any claim imposing non-monetary obligations on Company without Company's consent."

Also add an IP remedy: at Contractor's expense, procure the right to continue use, or replace/modify to be non-infringing while maintaining conformance to Specifications; refund only as a last resort.

### 3. IP ownership is conditional and there is no present assignment (¶4(a), ¶4(d), ¶6(b)/(c))
Works belong to Company only "to the extent … created … over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid." ¶4(a) says Works "are the property of Company" but contains **no assignment, no work-made-for-hire language, and no waiver of moral rights**. ¶4(d) further implies Company cannot modify the software until "paid in full." And ¶6(b) says Contractor assigns work-in-progress, while ¶11(c) — a stray subsection misnumbered under Governing Law — conditions that same assignment on "receipt of final payment." These conflict.

Practical risk: a good-faith invoice dispute leaves Company without title to deliverables it is actively using.

**Fix:**
- Delete the payment condition in ¶4(a) and the "after Company pays Contractor in full" condition in ¶4(d). Contractor's remedy for nonpayment should be a payment claim, not IP forfeiture.
- Add: "Contractor hereby irrevocably assigns to Company all right, title and interest, including all intellectual property rights, in and to the Works, effective upon creation. To the extent any Works constitute works made for hire under 17 U.S.C. § 101, they shall be deemed such. Contractor waives all moral rights in the Works."
- Add a fallback license so Company is never dark: "In the event of any dispute, Company retains an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, modify, and create derivative works of all Works delivered or in progress."
- Fix the ¶4(a) assistance clause: further-assurances cooperation should be at **Contractor's** cost where reasonably needed to perfect Company's rights, and should include a power of attorney if Contractor fails to execute.
- Reconcile the duplicate/conflicting termination-assignment provisions (¶6(b), ¶11(c)) — keep one, unconditional.

### 4. Contractor Information license is too narrow; ¶4(b)(ii) use restriction (¶4(c), ¶4(b))
The license to embedded Contractor Information omits **distribution and the right to have third parties exercise the rights on Company's behalf**, and is limited to "Company's business operations" — problematic if Clear Capital's deliverable is embedded in a product or service delivered to *its* customers, or if Company divests a business unit. ¶4(b)(ii) also bars Company from making "use of said property in any other manner other than in connection with the software Company receives."

**Fix:**
> "…a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid, non-exclusive license, with the right to sublicense, to use, copy, modify, create derivative works of, distribute, perform and display such Contractor Information, alone or as incorporated in the Works, for any purpose in connection with Company's and its affiliates' business, including permitting contractors, service providers, and successors to exercise these rights on Company's behalf."

Add: "Contractor shall not incorporate into the Works any open source software subject to a copyleft or reciprocal license without Company's prior written consent, and shall disclose all open source components in writing."

### 5. No data security, privacy, or data-return obligations
For a company in the real estate valuation/analytics space, this is the most conspicuous gap. There are no obligations regarding safeguards, breach notification, subprocessors, personnel background checks, use of production data, or return/destruction of Company data. GLBA/FCRA-adjacent data and any consumer PII may be in scope, plus state breach-notification statutes.

**Fix:** Add a Data Security and Privacy section (or Exhibit) covering: administrative, technical and physical safeguards consistent with a recognized framework; processing only as necessary to perform Services; no use of production/live data in development or test environments without written approval and de-identification; prohibition on offshore access without consent; breach notification within 24–48 hours with cooperation and remediation at Contractor's cost; return or certified destruction of Company data on termination or request; audit/assessment rights or annual SOC 2 Type II delivery; and flow-down to subcontractors. Confirm whether a DPA and/or GLBA service-provider addendum is needed.

### 6. SOW conflict order is inverted (¶1(a))
"In all instances of a conflict … the provisions of this Agreement shall control." This prevents Company from negotiating project-specific protections (higher caps, fixed fees, milestones, acceptance criteria, security terms) in a SOW.

**Fix:** "…the MSA shall control, except that a Statement of Work shall control to the extent it expressly identifies the MSA provision being modified and states the parties' intent to supersede it for that Statement of Work."

---

## Tier 2 — Significant Commercial and Operational Risk

### 7. Unilateral rate increases (¶3(b))
"Contractor reserves the right to change rates with 30 days notice." This overrides negotiated SOW pricing at will.

**Fix:** "Rates set forth in a Statement of Work are firm for the duration of that Statement of Work. Contractor may propose rate changes for new Statements of Work upon 90 days' written notice, effective no more frequently than annually and not exceeding [3%] or CPI, whichever is less."

### 8. Time-and-materials with no cap, no estimates, no audit (¶3(a), ¶3(b))
Compensation is T&M with no not-to-exceed amount, no obligation to notify when approaching estimate, and no right to withhold disputed amounts or audit records.

**Fix:** Add: each SOW must state a not-to-exceed amount that Contractor may not exceed without prior written authorization; Contractor to notify Company at 80% of the NTE; expenses reimbursable only if pre-approved in writing and compliant with Company's T&E policy; payment terms Net 45 from receipt of a conforming invoice; invoices submitted more than 90 days after Services rendered are waived; Company may withhold disputed amounts in good faith without breach; Company may audit Contractor's time and expense records for 24 months.

### 9. No acceptance procedure despite the heading (¶4)
Paragraph 4 is titled "…; ACCEPTANCE" but contains no acceptance mechanism, no testing period, and no remedy for deliverables that fail Specifications.

**Fix:** Add: "Company shall have [30] days from delivery to test each deliverable against the Specifications. Company may reject non-conforming deliverables with written notice describing the non-conformity; Contractor shall correct and redeliver within [10] business days at no additional charge. If a deliverable fails acceptance after [two] correction cycles, Company may (i) reject and receive a refund of amounts paid for that deliverable and dependent deliverables, or (ii) accept with an equitable fee reduction. Payment does not constitute acceptance."

### 10. Services warranty is missing / disclaimer is broad (¶1(b), ¶5(e))
The "professional and workmanlike manner" language sits in ¶1 as a covenant, not a warranty with a remedy. ¶5(e) then disclaims all implied warranties. ¶5(a) is qualified "to its knowledge" — legal compliance should be absolute. There is no warranty of conformance to Specifications, no malicious-code warranty, and no warranty period.

**Fix:**
- Delete "to its knowledge" in ¶5(a).
- Add: "Contractor warrants that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel in accordance with applicable industry standards; (ii) for [90] days after acceptance, the Works will conform to the Specifications and operate free of material defects; and (iii) the Works will be free of viruses, malware, back doors, disabling code, or other harmful code. Contractor's remedy obligation is to re-perform or correct at no charge; if it cannot do so within [30] days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work and receive a refund of fees paid for the non-conforming Services."
- Preserve non-infringement (¶5(c)) as an unqualified warranty — note it is currently well-drafted in Company's favor; keep it and resist any "to Contractor's knowledge" qualifier.

### 11. Change control lets Contractor veto but Company cannot stop work (¶1(d))
Contractor "shall not be bound by any change requested by Company, until such change has been accepted in writing by Contractor" — with no obligation to respond within any period and no Company right to stop or suspend.

**Fix:** Make it mutual: no change is binding on either party until signed by both; Contractor to respond to change requests with a written impact assessment within 5 business days; add Company's right to suspend Services under an SOW upon written notice, with fees only for Services performed prior to suspension.

### 12. Termination for convenience is illusory (¶6(a))
Termination for any reason is available only "at any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." Because the MSA continues until terminated and SOWs are the whole point, Company is effectively locked in for the life of every SOW with no exit.

**Fix:** Add: "Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience upon [30] days' written notice, in which case Company shall pay only for Services properly performed and non-cancellable expenses incurred through the termination date." Also add Company termination rights for: Contractor insolvency/bankruptcy/assignment for benefit of creditors; change of control of Contractor; and repeated failure to meet SOW milestones. Add a transition-assistance obligation (up to 60–90 days at then-current rates) with delivery of all Works, source code, documentation, credentials, and Company data.

### 13. Cure period is short and non-differentiated (¶6(b))
Fifteen days is fine for Company but also gives Contractor only 15 days to terminate for a payment dispute. Add: no termination for non-payment of amounts Company disputes in good faith and has notified Contractor of; payment breaches require written notice and a 15-day cure from notice.

### 14. Key Personnel protections are weak (¶1(b))
Contractor may substitute Key Personnel for any reason "beyond Contractor's reasonable control," and may add personnel it "determines to be required" — Company's approval right applies only "at Company's request," which is circular.

**Fix:** Contractor shall not remove or reassign Key Personnel without Company's prior written consent except due to death, disability, or resignation; replacements subject to Company's prior written approval with equal or better qualifications; no charge for ramp-up/knowledge transfer of replacement personnel. Company may require removal of any personnel from the engagement upon notice (not merely "cooperate to remedy"). Add background check and, where applicable, confidentiality-agreement requirements for all personnel with access to Company systems or data.

### 15. Third-party materials (¶1(f)) — good clause, but incomplete
¶1(f) helpfully puts functionality risk on Contractor. Add: Contractor must obtain and pay for all third-party licenses necessary for Company's use of the Works, disclose them in the SOW, and pass through all warranties and indemnities; no third-party terms bind Company without prior written consent.

---

## Tier 3 — Legal / Dispute Mechanics

### 16. Confidentiality is one-way and structurally deficient (¶8)
Only Contractor is bound; only information "obtained by Contractor from Company" is covered — so Contractor's *observations*, derived analyses, and Company information Contractor creates may be outside scope. Missing: standard-of-care obligation, need-to-know limitation, personnel/subcontractor flow-down, notice before compelled disclosure, no-residuals confirmation, return/destruction, survival period, and equitable relief. Note ¶12 references a separate Mutual NDA as part of the Agreement — confirm it exists, obtain a copy, and address any conflict.

**Fix:** Add: standard of care no less than reasonable care and no less than Contractor uses for its own confidential information; disclosure only to personnel with a need to know who are bound by written obligations at least as protective; prompt written notice and cooperation before compelled disclosure so Company may seek a protective order, and disclosure limited to the minimum required; return or destroy on request; obligations survive [5] years, and indefinitely for trade secrets and personal information; Company entitled to injunctive relief without bond. Confirm there is no "residuals" clause anywhere in the Mutual NDA.

### 17. Arbitration clause is problematic (¶19)
- The provider ("U.S. Arbitration & Mediation," identified by a URL) is not a major administrator; its rules are incorporated sight-unseen and may be amended unilaterally.
- No seat/venue, no number of arbitrators, no arbitrator qualifications, no allocation of fees.
- Scope is extraordinarily broad — "any previous or subsequent agreement" and "any other relationship, transaction or dealing between the parties," including disputes "arising before" the Agreement. This could sweep in unrelated matters.
- No carve-out allowing either party to seek injunctive relief in court for IP or confidentiality breaches — a serious gap given the Works and data at issue.
- Combined with ¶7(c)'s mutual attorneys' fee waiver, Company bears its own costs even in a clear-cut win.

**Fix:** Either (a) delete arbitration in favor of exclusive jurisdiction in courts in [Company's home venue] with a jury waiver, or (b) substitute AAA Commercial Rules (or JAMS), single arbitrator with relevant industry/technology experience, seat in [Company's venue], and add: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its intellectual property or Confidential Information." Narrow scope to disputes "arising out of or relating to this Agreement." Delete the ¶7(c) fee waiver or make fees awardable to the prevailing party.

### 18. Governing law and venue (¶11)
Arizona law ("the laws of the Arizona") with no venue designation, paired with an arbitration clause whose confirmation venue is defined by reference to the *residence of the party against whom the award was entered* — i.e., Company can be dragged to Contractor's home forum. Confirm whether Arizona is acceptable; otherwise change to Company's home state.

### 19. Assignment restriction blocks Company reorganizations (¶10)
Company cannot assign even to an affiliate or in a merger, and Contractor's consent standard ("not unreasonably withheld") still requires a negotiation at the worst possible moment.

**Fix:** "Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to an affiliate or in connection with a merger, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or of the business unit to which this Agreement relates. Contractor may not subcontract any portion of the Services without Company's prior written consent and remains fully responsible for the acts and omissions of any approved subcontractor."

### 20. Force majeure is over-broad (¶15)
"Failure of suppliers" and "any other reason where failure to perform is beyond the control of the nonperforming party" are too generous, and there is no time limit or Company termination right.

**Fix:** Delete "failure of suppliers"; require the affected party to use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and resume; add: "If a force majeure event continues for more than [30] consecutive days, Company may terminate the affected Statement of Work without liability other than for Services properly performed prior to the event." Confirm force majeure does not excuse Contractor's confidentiality or data security obligations.

### 21. Insurance limits and structure (¶14)
$1M CGL and $1M E&O are low for a technology/data engagement, and there is **no cyber liability / technology E&O coverage** and no requirement that Company be named additional insured or that the policies be primary and non-contributory.

**Fix:** CGL $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate; Professional Liability/Technology E&O $2–5M including cyber liability, network security, privacy liability, and breach response costs; Workers' Comp per statute plus Employer's Liability $1M; commercial auto if applicable; umbrella as appropriate. Add: insurers rated A- or better; Company named additional insured on CGL; waiver of subrogation; coverage primary and non-contributory; 30 days' notice of cancellation or material change; certificates delivered at signing and annually. Also add: "Maintenance of insurance does not limit Contractor's liability under this Agreement."

### 22. Non-solicitation is mutual — check impact (¶13)
Mutual and reasonably scoped, but note it bars Company from *hiring* Contractor personnel who worked on the Services for one year post-termination. If Company might want to bring key developers in-house, negotiate a carve-out for general solicitations (job postings, recruiters not targeted at the other party) and for individuals who apply unsolicited or who left the other party more than [6] months prior. Also confirm enforceability of any such restriction under applicable law.

### 23. Tax gross-up is broad (¶3(c))
Company bears "other applicable taxes, tariffs or duties." Add: Company is not responsible for taxes based on Contractor's income, gross receipts, property, payroll, or employment; Contractor is responsible for penalties and interest arising from its failure to timely invoice or remit; Contractor shall separately state taxes on invoices and cooperate in claiming exemptions.

### 24. Drafting cleanups
- **Duplicate/conflicting clauses:** ¶11 (Severability; Governing Law) vs. ¶18 (Severability); ¶12 (Integration) vs. ¶17 (Entire Agreement). ¶17 says the Agreement is the "complete and exclusive agreement," which conflicts with ¶12's inclusion of the Mutual NDA and SOWs, and refers to "this project" (singular) and "Consultant." **Delete ¶17 and ¶18**; retain ¶11 and ¶12 as amended.
- **Misnumbered stray subsection:** ¶11(c) (termination payment/assignment) belongs in ¶6 and conflicts with ¶6(b). Resolve.
- **"Consultant" vs. "Contractor":** ¶4(d) and ¶17 use "Consultant," an undefined term. Conform to "Contractor."
- **"a time and materials"** (¶3(a)) is incomplete — should read "on a time and materials basis" and cross-reference the SOW.
- **Missing survival clause.** Add: "Paragraphs 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, and [new indemnity, data security] survive termination or expiration."
- **No notices provision.** Add addresses, permitted methods, and deemed-receipt rules.
- **No records/audit right.** Covered above for fees; consider a general compliance audit right.
- **No compliance/records obligations** for the anti-corruption covenant (¶5(d)) — add an audit right and a representation regarding sanctions/export controls and debarment lists if relevant.
- **No SOW template or minimum contents.** Add a required-elements list (scope, deliverables, Specifications, acceptance criteria, schedule/milestones, Key Personnel, NTE amount, rates, assumptions, dependencies).
- **Signature block** shows Michael Rockford signing "for RadialSpark" and John Marcum "for Clear Capital" — confirm signatory authority and titles, and confirm the correct legal entity name for Clear Capital (e.g., "Clear Capital, LLC" / "Clear Capital.com, Inc.").
- **¶5(d) forfeiture:** the anti-corruption clause states Company "shall have no obligation to pay any fees" upon such termination. This is favorable to Company but may be challenged as a penalty; it is worth keeping, but do not rely on it as the sole remedy.

---

## Suggested Negotiation Priorities

| # | Issue | Position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Present assignment of IP; remove payment condition (¶4) | Must have |
| 2 | Contractor indemnity for IP, confidentiality, data breach, GN/WM (new) | Must have |
| 3 | Fix cap carve-outs; supercap for data/confidentiality breach (¶7) | Must have |
| 4 | Data security, privacy, breach notification, data return (new) | Must have |
| 5 | Delete unilateral rate change (¶3(b)) | Must have |
| 6 | Termination for convenience + transition assistance (¶6) | Must have |
| 7 | SOWs may supersede MSA where expressly stated (¶1(a)) | Must have |
| 8 | Acceptance testing and remedies (¶4) | Strong ask |
| 9 | Services/deliverable/malicious-code warranties + warranty period (¶5) | Strong ask |
| 10 | Arbitration: AAA/JAMS, Company venue, IP/confidentiality court carve-out; delete fee waiver (¶19, ¶7(c)) | Strong ask |
| 11 | Insurance: add cyber/tech E&O, raise limits, additional insured (¶14) | Strong ask |
| 12 | NTE caps, expense pre-approval, payment terms, dispute withholding, audit (¶3) | Strong ask |
| 13 | Assignment carve-out for affiliates/M&A; subcontractor consent + responsibility (¶10) | Strong ask |
| 14 | Key Personnel consent and replacement standards (¶1(b)) | Trade |
| 15 | Broader Contractor Information license; open source restrictions (¶4(b)–(c)) | Trade |
| 16 | Mutual confidentiality; strengthen ¶8 mechanics | Trade |
| 17 | Narrow force majeure; 30-day termination right (¶15) | Trade |
| 18 | Governing law/venue to Company's state (¶11) | Trade |
| 19 | Survival, notices, drafting cleanups (¶¶11, 12, 17, 18, misc.) | Housekeeping |

---

**Two diligence items before signing:** (i) obtain and review the referenced **Mutual Non-Disclosure Agreement** — it is incorporated by ¶12 and may contain a residuals clause, a shorter survival period, or conflicting terms; and (ii) confirm whether any **existing SOWs** have already been executed, since they may contain terms this MSA purports to override under ¶1(a).

*This review reflects general market practice for customer-side technology services agreements. It is not a substitute for confirming your organization's specific approval thresholds, insurance requirements, and regulatory obligations (including any GLBA, FCRA, or state privacy law requirements applicable to Clear Capital's data), and any final positions should be validated with the business owner and, where relevant, outside counsel in the governing jurisdiction.*
